The very first thing to try always is to turn off bit defenders anti-spam tools

Not the 1 - 5 you have listed. They come after you eliminate the obvious culprit which is always the antivirus these days. If Thunderbird did have such an issue this forum would be full of folk complaining, but like all update times there are a few that have paid for antivirus products that only sort of work in a single version of Thunderbird.

did you read the support article? https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/protect-your-thunderbird-passwords-primary-password

That password only protect your passwords nothing else. Pressing escape on the keyboard will remove the initial request but the password manager will not be able to access your passwords until you either enter it or remove it. but that is all discussed in some detail in the support article.
